subject: Promotion packet — exception window and evidence shortfall (confidential)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Promotion packet — exception window and evidence shortfall (confidential)

Hi Markus / Grace,

I'm attaching Maya's promotion packet (v3) for review — she's being considered for Senior PM, promotion cycle 2027Q2. Two quick asks: one operational, one policy.

1) Evidence shortfall: the packet is otherwise strong, but we've only got one recent customer reference that speaks to scale rollout impact. The account contact (Amanda at SampleSoft) has provided a short testimonial but it includes a customer's internal metrics slide that our standard blackout would normally omit. I've attached customer_testimonials_redacted.docx which removes direct PII but still includes the high-level metric statements.

2) Committee window: the nominations slate closes next Friday (5/14). The next promotions committee meeting with available slots is 5/18, but Maya's manager is leaving on parental leave the week after, so we need either a canary slot this week or an explicit exception to accept the redacted customer evidence.

Requested: can you confirm (a) whether we can accept the redacted external testimony as-is under an exception, and (b) if not, whether we can secure a canary committee slot before 5/14 so the packet isn't delayed?

Attachments: maya_promotion_packet_draft_v3.pdf, customer_testimonials_redacted.docx

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

---
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Promotion packet — exception window and evidence shortfall (confidential)

Karthik —

Thanks for the packet. Quick read: Maya's impact narrative and cross-functional letters look solid. Two notes from my side:

- Policy: we generally avoid customer metrics with proprietary percentage deltas even if redacted; the security/legal committee looks for first-party attestations (i.e., customer-signed letter on company letterhead). That said, if SampleSoft can provide a short signed letter that avoids raw metrics (e.g., "improved onboarding time and increased API throughput") instead of slide screenshots, we could accept it without an exception.
- Calendar: there is a small internal conflict for committee reviewers on 5/18 (quarterly kickoff planning). I can try to open a 45-minute canary slot on 5/13 afternoon if people can commit.

If we need to escalate for an exception, this would be a People Ops decision (Lauren). Can you loop Lauren and capture the specific redactions you've made and why metrics are critical for Maya's case?

—Markus

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Promotion packet — exception window and evidence shortfall (confidential)

Lauren — forwarding for exception review.

Context: Maya (PM on Search Infra) has a promotion packet that hinges on a delivery where she led a cross-org API optimization. The customer (SampleSoft) provided a slide with before/after metrics. Legal and Markus are uncomfortable with ingesting that slide intact. We redacted the slide and distilled it into a one-paragraph written testimony that omits all customer PII and exact percent numbers; still argues the magnitude of impact in qualitative terms.

Why policy exception? The committee historically weighs quantifiable impact heavily — without a customer-attested numeric anchor, some reviewers feel the case weakens materially. Maya will be out of manager sponsorship timeline if we miss the slate this cycle.

Attached: maya_promotion_packet_draft_v3.pdf; customer_testimonials_redacted.docx; evidence_checklist_promotions.xls

Please advise whether People Ops can grant a limited exception to accept the redacted written testimony for committee review, and if so, any required caveats (e.g., store the original in the HR evidence vault with restricted access, require customer-signed waiver).

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Promotion packet — exception window and evidence shortfall (confidential)

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the detailed write-up and attachments. A couple clarifying questions before I rule on an exception:

1) Can we confirm SampleSoft is happy with the redacted letter and will sign it? If they will not sign, we cannot accept second-hand metric claims.
2) Please provide the minimal list of fields removed from the original slide (e.g., customer name, account IDs, raw % change) so People Ops & Legal can assess residual reidentification risk.

Operationally: I can approve an exception that allows the redacted written testimony for committee review if we meet three conditions:
- The original metric slide is stored in the HR evidence vault (encrypted) and only accessible to People Ops + Legal for audit (retention policy: 5 years).
- The submitted packet includes a one-sentence addendum stating the customer has authorized use of the redacted content for internal promotion review only.
- Mateo (Legal) signs off within 48 hours — I'll ping Legal now.

On the committee slot: I can liaise with Scheduling to try to secure the 5/13 2:00–2:45pm canary slot Markus mentioned. If the slot can't be confirmed by EOD 5/10, we will need to move the nomination to the next slate.

Please reply with confirmation from SampleSoft and a short summary of which fields were removed.

—Lauren
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference

---
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Promotion packet — exception window and evidence shortfall (confidential)

Looping in an operational confirmation: I spoke with Amanda at SampleSoft this morning. They agreed to sign the redacted one-paragraph testimony and confirmed they are comfortable with the edits — they explicitly asked that internal account IDs be removed and that we not share any record-level logs. Amanda will send the signed letter before EOD 5/9; she requested we reference "SampleSoft (customer)" generically in the addendum, not the account-specific name.

Attached: customer_testimonials_redacted.docx (updated with Amanda's signature placeholder).

Karthik — I also opened a Scheduling request for 5/13 14:00–14:45 as a canary. I'll update when confirmed.

—Monica
Senior People Ops Partner
Redwood Inference

---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Promotion packet — exception window and evidence shortfall (confidential)

Confirmed: I've reviewed the redactions Monica described and Legal responded with conditional signoff (JIRA-LEGAL-4492). People Ops grants a limited exception to accept the redacted signed testimony for committee review on the following conditions:

- Original slide retained in HR evidence vault, encrypted, access limited to People Ops and Legal.
- Packet addendum wording: "SampleSoft (customer) has authorized the use of this redacted testimony for internal promotion review only."
- Evidence retention flagged for 5 years; any external audit requests must go through Legal.

Monica — please upload the signed letter to the Drive folder (link below) and move the canary slot request to confirmed if Scheduling approves. Markus / Grace — please treat the attachment as confidential and do not forward outside the review committee.

Scheduling update: Scheduling has confirmed the 5/13 14:00–14:45 canary slot. Markus, please ensure the reviewers get the packet by EOD 5/11 so they have 48 hours to digest.

Thanks all — exception approved. I'll add the JIRA entry and close the loop.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-promotions/maya_packet
JIRA: JIRA-HR-7289 (promotion exception)

—Lauren

Redwood Inference
